verses.text: Family, my heart’s desire—and my prayer to God—is for Israel to be saved.
I can vouch for them: they’re fired up for God, but they don’t have the right understanding.
They didn’t understand how God makes people righteous, and tried to set up their own way instead. They wouldn’t submit to God’s way of making people right.
Christ is the goal of the Law, so everyone who believes can be made right with God.
Moses writes that the person who does what the Law says will live by it.
But faith’s way of righteousness says, “Don’t say in your heart, ‘Who’s going up to heaven?’”—as if you had to bring Christ down—
“or, ‘Who’s going down into the abyss?’”—as if you had to bring Christ back from the dead.
So what does it say? “The message is right here with you—in your mouth and in your heart.” That’s the message of faith we preach:
If you say with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” and trust in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you’ll be saved.
Trusting in the heart makes a person right with God; saying it aloud brings salvation.
Scripture says, “Everyone who trusts in him won’t be put to shame.”
There’s no VIP line for Jews or Greeks. The same Lord is Lord of everyone, and he generously helps everyone who calls on him.
Scripture says, “Everyone who calls on the Lord’s name will be saved.”
But how can people call on someone they haven’t trusted? How can they trust someone they haven’t heard about? And how can they hear without someone preaching?
How can anyone preach unless they’re sent? Scripture says, “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring the Good News of peace and announce good things!” 👣
But not everybody took the Good News to heart. Isaiah says, “Lord, who believed what we told them?”
So faith comes from hearing the message, and the message comes through Christ’s word.
But didn’t they hear? They did: “Their sound went through the whole earth; their words reached the ends of the world.”
But didn’t Israel understand? First Moses says, “I’ll make you jealous through a people who aren’t even a nation; I’ll make you angry through a people who don’t understand.”
Then Isaiah speaks boldly: “I was found by people who weren’t looking for me. I showed myself to people who weren’t asking for me.”
But about Israel, he says, “All day long I held out my hands to a disobedient, stubborn people.”
